hints: Focus on what functional group actually undergoes nucleophilic addition with HCN in a 1:1 ratio.
For formula $C_5H_{10}O$, that means you are counting only aldehydes and ketones, so start by listing the 4 possible aldehydes with 5 carbons.
Now list the ketone skeletons separately and check carefully for duplicates caused by numbering from either end, then add the two totals together.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reacting group**

Great start, let us decode the clue. HCN adds by nucleophilic addition in a 1:1 ratio only to the $C=O$ of aldehydes and ketones.

Reaction type:
$$R_2C=O + HCN \rightarrow R_2C(OH)CN$$

**Count the aldehyde isomers**

An aldehyde is $R-CHO$, so the $CHO$ carbon is C1 and we arrange the other 4 carbons. There are 4 structural options.

$$pentanal, 2\text{-}methylbutanal, 3\text{-}methylbutanal, 2,2\text{-}dimethylpropanal$$

**Count the ketone isomers**

A ketone is $R-CO-R'$, so place $C=O$ inside a 5-carbon skeleton. There are only 3 distinct options.

$$pentan\text{-}2\text{-}one, pentan\text{-}3\text{-}one, 3\text{-}methylbutan\text{-}2\text{-}one$$

**Add to get the set**

Notice that 2-methylbutan-3-one is the same molecule as 3-methylbutan-2-one, just numbered from the other end, so do not count it twice. Total reacting isomers is aldehydes plus ketones.

$$Total = 4 + 3 = 7$$

options.A: 5 is too low. It usually comes from counting only straight-chain and simply branched isomers and missing highly branched ones like 2,2-dimethylpropanal and 3-methylbutan-2-one.
options.B: 6 is one short. Students often find the 4 aldehydes but count only 2 ketones, forgetting the branched ketone 3-methylbutan-2-one.
options.C: 7 is correct: 4 aldehydes (pentanal, 2-methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal, 2,2-dimethylpropanal) plus 3 ketones (pentan-2-one, pentan-3-one, 3-methylbutan-2-one). All have $C=O$ and undergo 1:1 nucleophilic addition with HCN.
options.D: 8 is one too many. It comes from double-counting 3-methylbutan-2-one as 2-methylbutan-3-one, which are the same structural isomer numbered from opposite ends.
